backing: D-320 backs the scalar check on `Model(deployment, T)` only. D-254 (the composed forms defined as the composition) backs the code's order. The alternative is a code change that checks T first in the composed forms, so the fix is a choice.
claim: Appendix C says the scalar refusal comes 'alone and before the keywords are read', and the docstring says 'before anything is compiled'. fix: Appendix C: '`Model(deployment, T)` at a scalar other than `Float64` or a concrete `ForwardDiff.Dual` over `Float64`, nested or not, raises it with reason `:scalar`, alone and before its keywords are read ([D-320]). The composed forms build the deployment first, so its refusals come ahead of the scalar's.' ver_evidence: src/model.jl:129-132: Model(build, T; chunk_size, kw...) = Model(Deployment(build; kw...), T; chunk_size), and Model(root, T; kw...) = Model(build(root), T; kw...), so the deployment (and the build) are evaluated before the scalar check at src/model.jl:111. Model(root, Float32; Δt_frame=-1) gives DeploymentInvalid. A root that fails to build, at Float32, gives PathResolution + UnconnectedInput. Model(dep, Float32; chunk_size=0) gives :scalar alone, so the claim holds for the deployment form only.
ver_note: For the root form, build(root) runs the whole build pipeline, including the nominal Float64 activation, before the refusal. So the docstring's 'before anything is compiled' is also too broad there.

claim: A feedback loop closed through B is schedulable precisely because B's output is held state rather than feedthrough (§5.3)
fix: A feedback loop closed through B is schedulable when B publishes the looped output from `y_state`, held state rather than feedthrough ([§5.3][s5-3]). A loop through B's `y_direct` is feedthrough in the boundary sweep, on the discrete tier as on the continuous one, and [§5.5][s5-5] rejects it as algebraic.
ver_evidence: src/build.jl:199-213 (`_outputs`) adds a feedthrough edge for every consumed stage-2 port on either tier, with no tier test. Probe 'K9b-014': a loop through a discrete component's `y_direct` is refused as AlgebraicCycle :real. The same loop through UnitDelay, whose output comes from y_state, builds.
ver_note: The doc says the framework does not treat a discrete y_direct as in-sweep feedthrough. The code, and spec §5.3's D-006 sentence ('every stage-2 output is presumed dependent on every wired input'), do treat it so. No log entry backs the doc's reading.

claim: Pinning the moving deck's output would silently zero the coupling between ship motion and touchdown
fix: Pinning here would zero the coupling between ship motion and touchdown. The stage would then have to strip the pose's partials, and as written it is refused as `ConformanceFailure` at the build's `Dual` probe.
ver_evidence: probe 'K9b-027': the moving deck declared `Pinned{DeckField{Float64}}`, with the walkthrough's y_state, is refused at build as ConformanceFailure (y_state, :field_type, got DeckField{Dual}, declared DeckField{Float64}). The pin fails loudly. The coupling goes to zero silently only if the author also strips the pose's partials.

[D-263][d-263]'s rule that a mutable type's parameters pin covers only a grid type carried as a parameter. The one-scalar-plus-reference shape gets the same derivatives for free.

The mutable rule only pins a grid type carried as a parameter: H{Matrix{Float64}} stays H{Matrix{Float64}}.
ver_note: Spec §8.2 (spec.md:3228-3230, 3248-3249) makes the same attribution ('That is the copy the mutable-parameter rule above refuses'), so the fix also reaches the spec.

claim: D-136: a noisy frame allocates a fresh ring lazily, once, at the writer's next emission after a drain.
fix: each emission the ring accepts allocates a fresh copy of the ring (the CAS handoff's value semantics), so a noisy frame allocates up to sixteen rings of growing length per writer
ver_evidence: src/dataplane.jl:141-150: report_cell! builds DiagBatch(push!(copy(current.ring), occurrence), ...) at every accepted emission. Probe: emissions 1 to 16 after a drain allocated 112, 160, ..., 576 bytes each, and emissions 17 to 20 allocated 0.
ver_note: The DiagBatch docstring (src/dataplane.jl:100-103) states the copy-on-append choice, so the copy is deliberate. Nothing in the log or pending records it. The alternative fix is code that appends in place to a ring allocated once per frame.

claim: D-136: the worst case per writer per boundary is one ring of 16, and everything past it is an integer increment.
fix: the worst case per writer per boundary is sixteen ring copies of growing length, the last holding sixteen values, and everything past the ring is an integer increment
ver_evidence: Probe: past the ring, emissions 17 to 20 allocated 0 bytes, so the integer-increment half holds. Up to the bound, sixteen ring copies of lengths 1 to 16 were allocated (about 5.6 KB), not one ring of 16 (src/dataplane.jl:144-145).

fix: at the stage-return seam the framework pairs fields by name in the write generated over the return type, one getfield per declared port
ver_evidence: src/store.jl:107-129: the seam has no NamedTuple{canonical_names}(y) reorder. The generated write pairs by name with getfield(y, name) per declared port, decided on the return type.
ver_note: D-235 moved the check and the pairing into the generated write.

claim: D-151: §9.5 keeps one whole-type `isa` against the declared type, never per-field checks.
fix: §9.5's check is decided per field at the generated write, against the cell types, with no per-field instruction at runtime
ver_evidence: src/store.jl:102-123: the always-on check is a key-set compare plus a per-field _accepts(declared, observed, T), evaluated at generation. No whole-type isa remains.
ver_note: D-235 records it: 'D-053's rejection of per-field checks holds in the sense it was made, which is cost.'

claim: D-253: the tracer takes its name lists from `Structure` and `Dataflow`, never from an activation.
fix: the tracer takes its name lists from `Structure` and the nominal evaluation's own declarations, never from an activation
